title: Pak Choi with Oyster Sauce
subtitle: Blanched pak choi with a garlic and oyster sauce dressing
excerpt: Blanched pak choi with oyster sauce is one of the most fundamental Chinese vegetable dishes: tender pak choi briefly blanched in boiling water, then dressed with a sauce of oyster sauce, sesame oil, and fried garlic. It takes 10 minutes and serves as a side dish for any Chinese meal.
sourceNotes: Blanched greens with oyster sauce (hao you cai xin) is a cornerstone of Cantonese cooking. The combination of the savoury oyster sauce, sesame oil, and fried garlic over tender blanched green vegetables appears on virtually every Chinese restaurant menu. Any leafy Chinese green can be used: gai lan (Chinese broccoli), choy sum, or bok choy all work.

content.text: Blanch the pak choi briefly: 1 to 2 minutes maximum, depending on size. The leaves should be bright green and just tender; the stems should retain a slight bite. Adding a little oil to the blanching water keeps the colour vivid.

items.prepNote: 1 tsp in blanching water, rest for frying garlic

content.text: Bring a large pan of water to a rolling boil. Add a teaspoon of oil and a pinch of salt. Blanch the pak choi halves for 1 to 2 minutes until the leaves are wilted and bright green and the stalks are just tender. Drain and arrange on a serving plate.
Mix the oyster sauce, soy sauce, sesame oil, and sugar. Spoon over the warm pak choi.

Heat the remaining sunflower oil in a small pan over medium-high heat until shimmering. Add the sliced garlic and fry for 30 to 45 seconds until just golden. Pour immediately over the pak choi. Serve at once.

items.symptom: Pak choi is yellow rather than bright green
items.cause: Blanched too long, or the lid was on the pan
items.fix: 1 to 2 minutes maximum. Do not cover the pan. Drain and serve immediately.
